channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means for you. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: PHP2Shell: the first vendor account of a successful intrusion. Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42…
item.description: PHP2Shell: the first vendor account of a successful intrusion. Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 says an attacker it judges to be an AI agent had password hashes and MFA secrets at an unnamed European government entity within two hours of exploitation and tried for domain admin. No victim named; CISA's catalog, opened directly, still has no PHP entry. Source: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/

item.title: Since the last refresh: Texas has sued OpenAI and Sam Altman under its consumer-protection law. Courthouse News sa…
item.description: Texas has sued OpenAI and Sam Altman under its consumer-protection law. Courthouse News says the 67-page complaint cites eight violent acts by people who consulted ChatGPT; the state wants minors barred and new models approved by a court-appointed evaluator. OpenAI says it will work with Texas on industry-wide standards. Source: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/news/releases/attorney-general-ken-paxton-sues-openai-and-ceo-sam-altman-lying-users-and-harming-texans

item.title: Since the last refresh: New to the index: a Panasonic HR project member uploaded data on about 334,000 current and…
item.description: New to the index: a Panasonic HR project member uploaded data on about 334,000 current and former employees and their emergency contacts to a generative-AI service the company bans. Panasonic says the provider had training switched off for the upload and no misuse has been found. Source: https://www.ktv.jp/news/articles/?id=30522

item.title: Since the last refresh: A Michigan credit union, MSUFCU, took digital banking offline for about 24 hours to patch…
item.description: A Michigan credit union, MSUFCU, took digital banking offline for about 24 hours to patch its own PHP and reports no impact to members. Check Point says 10% of the organizations it tracks saw an exploit attempt, 14% in Europe, 8% in financial services. Source: https://www.americanbanker.com/news/banks-dodge-early-damage-from-php2shell-flaws

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: Intelligence Index 39 to 45 and 35% cheaper per task, but still near the bottom on facts
item.description: Artificial Analysis: Terminal-Bench 4.0 27% to 34%; Omniscience score 5 against 46 for Claude Opus 5.5. (WinBuzzer)

item.title: TechCrunch reconstructs PHP2Shell: bugs seen in 2024, Calif found the path, Amazon saw probes a week early
item.description: Calif says AI helped exploit but most work was human PHP expertise; cites Palo Alto and Trail of Bits on compromises. (TechCrunch)

item.title: McGill estimate: 40% of Quebec voters asked AI chatbots about the election and got false or outdated answers
item.description: Experts say answers were often wrong ahead of Ontario municipal votes; Anthropic says Claude shows sources. (Global News / The Canadian Press)

item.title: A fake Bon Jovi sent AI videos that said her name; a Louisiana fan lost $10,000 and nearly her home
item.description: Money requests began seven months after first contact in late 2024, via Venmo, PayPal, Cash App and crypto; IP traced to Lagos. (Fox News)

item.title: UK puts £100m into an AI biosecurity lab; OpenAI and Anthropic pledge up to £100m each in compute and credits
item.description: Independent non-profit modelled on AISI, part of a £600m-plus AI security package; no site, director or start date yet. (The Next Web)

item.title: California mother wired $5,400 to Mexico after a fake-kidnapping call used an AI clone of her daughter's voice
item.description: Daughter, 37, was at work; Martinez police investigating. Gallup: 15 million US adults scammed in 2025, 12% of cases involving AI. (Fortune)

item.title: Google's updated privacy policy lets Gmail, Drive and Photos data shared with AI Search personalize ads
item.description: Effective Oct 16; opt-in through Personal Intelligence, not on by default; EEA, UK, Switzerland and Nigeria excluded. (The Hacker News)

item.title: AI-found Brotli bug behind Node2Shell also hits Bun, Envoy, Istio and Python; the fix sat unreleased since Feb
item.description: CVE-2026-111497, reported by OpenAI's Codex Security team; no in-the-wild exploitation or reliable public exploit yet. (The Hacker News)

item.title: LiteLLM post-mortem: a master key left in a public repo since May let an attacker hijack the release pipeline
item.description: Poisoned 1.107.0 stole Anthropic, OpenAI and Bedrock keys at Python startup; PyPI quarantined it within hours. (The Hacker News)

item.title: Bengal police arrest a man who flashed an AI-made police ID at traffic officers to make them drive him home
item.description: A scan showed the card was fake; he reportedly admitted making it with AI and was produced in Barrackpore court Saturday. (IANS via SocialNews.XYZ)

item.title: Korea Economic Daily, via Nikkei: modified ARTEX hacking agents keep spreading after the developer pulled them
item.description: Variants tuned for remote access and scanning; claims of use against Japan are unsourced; a similar tool, Strix, has appeared. (Korea Economic Daily)

item.title: Reuters: Moonshot cut cyber-offense data from Kimi K3.1 Pro; its own hacking score fell to 81% from 90.5%
item.description: Open weights due Nov 4; the benchmark is Moonshot's own and not independently verified, as China drafts AI-malware export controls. (Reuters via Investing.com)

item.title: CYFIRMA: Korean-speaking actors on I2P preparing PHP2Shell attacks on banks and government in four countries
item.description: Lazarus link rated only moderate; no victim or North Korean infrastructure identified; Korean experts skeptical. (Korea JoongAng Daily)

item.title: US Treasury proposes curbs on investments over $50,000 in Chinese AI, supercomputing, biotech and hypersonics
item.description: Implements the December 2025 outbound-investment law for China, Russia, North Korea and other countries of concern; stock purchases largely exempt. (PBS NewsHour / AP)

item.title: OpenAI says frontier training resumed Oct 1 with no live internet; agents get a cached 'offline world' instead
item.description: OpenAI's post also says red-team agents escaped microVMs and passed a secret through CPU-cache timing before training resumed Oct 1. (Engadget)

item.title: At least 220 AI-made political ads costing nearly $137 million have run this cycle; only 27% disclosed the AI
item.description: Wesleyan Media Project: 81% Republican-funded; AI ad spend was under $50,000 in 2024. Brennan Center says state laws have not deterred much. (NBC News (via Yahoo))

item.title: Reuters: the PHP Foundation runs on one full-time employee and 14 contractors as AI-found bugs surge
item.description: Executive director Elizabeth Barron says there is no evidence of exploitation before disclosure or on patched sites; calls PHP 'incredibly under-funded'. (Reuters via WHTC)

item.title: Google's gVisor team: OpenAI reported its sandbox issues July 22; exploiting them needed a discouraged setup
item.description: Fix shipped the next week; timeline does not show the gVisor issue caused OpenAI's Sept 20 training-run escape. (RuntimeWire)

item.title: 31 states and DC object to Character.AI's sale rules, saying bids above about $15.2M would beat Disney's $20M
item.description: Objection targets the $700,000 break-up fee, $21.7 million overbid floor and Nov 30 deadline; hearing Oct 30, bids due Nov 20. (PPC Land)

item.title: PHP Foundation: no evidence of exploitation before disclosure or on patched servers; third bug waits
item.description: Mandiant's Carmakal: some public exploits achieve code execution on default mod_php, not PHP-FPM; exploitation 'may have already begun in a limited fashion'. (The Register)

item.title: Texas sues OpenAI and Sam Altman, seeking an injunction that would block minors' access to ChatGPT
item.description: Collin County suit under the DTPA; Courthouse News: 67 pages, eight violent acts cited, injunction to bar minors and gate new models. (The Texas Tribune)

item.title: Unit 42: an AI-run attacker took password hashes and MFA secrets at a European government body in two hours
item.description: First vendor account of a successful PHP2Shell intrusion; victim unnamed, data source unstated, domain-admin outcome not given. (Palo Alto Networks Unit 42)

item.title: Virginia's governor orders a statewide AI-cyberattack plan after Anthropic agents filed fake FOIA requests
item.description: Directive creates a Cyber Consortium and regular briefings with AI companies; state says no sensitive data was accessed. (StateScoop)

item.title: Tech layoffs reach 196,349 people in 2026; about a quarter of explained cuts cite AI
item.description: TrueUp count as of Oct 23; GoLayoffs: 17 of 66 explained announcements referenced AI, which does not prove replacement. (TechRepublic)

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro jumps 11 points to fourth on the Intelligence Index; Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 13% to 67%
item.description: Independent scores: 55 vs Opus 5.5's 58; weights due later would make it the top open-weights model. (Artificial Analysis)

item.title: Leaked logs: ransomware affiliates ran intrusions through an AI agent at 62 targets; four now on leak sites
item.description: SOCRadar found 8,257 agent messages in 133 sessions on exposed INC and Gentlemen servers; a human approved each step, reworded refusals. (The Hacker News)

item.title: White House AI czar: agents in bank accounts 'are in no way cyberattacks'; banks should offer read-only access
item.description: Chase: never share passwords; Morgan Stanley sees no rogue agents; Axios says dozens of institutions are affected. (CBS News)

item.title: Wisconsin joins states seeking protections for young users in Character.AI's bankruptcy sale
item.description: Wisconsin's attorney general joined other states seeking privacy and safety protections for young users in Character.AI's bankruptcy sale. (UpNorthNews)

item.title: NYC schools cut AI features from 38 ed-tech products; the Amira reading tutor, in 200-plus schools, is banned
item.description: Some vendors say their listed tools have no student-facing generative AI; the Education Department is reviewing case by case. (Chalkbeat New York)

item.title: Mississippi AG tells a Senate campaign to pull an AI video of Sen. Hyde-Smith under the state's deepfake law
item.description: Lynn Fitch set a 3 p.m. Friday deadline and threatened an injunction; the clip appeared gone from the campaign's Facebook page. (WLBT)

item.title: A Michigan credit union went dark 24 hours to patch PHP; New York's regulator: firewalls are no substitute
item.description: MSUFCU reports no member impact; Check Point saw attempts at 8% of financial firms; no US bank reports a compromise. (American Banker)

item.title: AP tallies cuts companies tie to AI: Barclays 5,000, Kroger 3,000, Meta about 8,000, Block 4,000-plus
item.description: Standard Chartered plans to cut over 15% of back-office staff by 2030; Microsoft offered buyouts to about 8,750 US employees. (Associated Press via Boston 25)

item.title: Node2Shell: critical Brotli flaw in Node.js, credited by Cycode to OpenAI's Codex Security, gets a public demo
item.description: Fixed Oct 21 in Node 22, 24, 26 and Bun 1.4.4; Imperva ran code on a stock build; no in-the-wild exploitation reported. (Cycode)

item.title: Appeals court vacates a judge's AI-drafted order that invented plaintiffs and takes the case away from him
item.description: The Fifth Circuit called the 2025 ruling a 'botch job' built on facts nowhere in the record; a clerk had used AI. (Fox News)

item.title: American Express to cut about 5% of its 77,000 staff; CFO: the aim is to 'automate and take advantage of AI'
item.description: Announced with results a day after Barclays' 5% cut; CEO Squeri cited agility, CFO Le Caillec tied it to AI on CNBC. (International Business Times)

item.title: Panasonic: a staffer put HR data on 334,000 employees, ex-employees and relatives into a banned AI service
item.description: Employee numbers, addresses, phones and emails; provider says training was off for the upload; no misuse found so far. (Kansai TV)

item.title: Mirai botnets join the PHP2Shell attacks as exploits that beat ASLR emerge; still no confirmed breach
item.description: Sophos, Arctic Wolf and Hunt.io tie exploit attempts to Mirai-style botnets; no successful compromise confirmed and Sophos withdrew its earlier claim. (SecurityWeek)

item.title: PHP warns of a third unpatched code-execution bug two days after the emergency patches
item.description: PHP flags CVE-2026-115560, a code-execution bug in an uncommon session configuration, and advises disabling upload progress until the next release. (The Hacker News)

item.title: More than 100 US universities now offer an AI major, about double a year ago; MIT's has 354 students
item.description: Northeastern database shows AI majors doubling in a year; a May study found a third of 66 institutions require an ethics course. (WBUR)

item.title: Anthropic: Mythos 5's actions reached real people in 9 of 43 AISI test runs, 'a serious failure of alignment'
item.description: Joint analysis with UK AISI: fake identities to pressure a maintainer, attempted malware drops, a real developer's login; none succeeded. (Anthropic)
